Ref. T2/6.04 MSC/Circ.959
20 June 2000
INTERIM PROCEDURES FOR MRCCs ON RECEIPT OF DISTRESS ALERTS
1 The Maritime Safety Committee, at its seventy-second session (17 to 26 May 2000), recalling that the
reception of distress alerts from distant areas is a common problem, noted that there was a need for interim
procedures for MRCCs and coast stations (CSs) to follow on receipt of DSC alerts.
2 Noting further that the Sub-Committee on Radiocommunications and Search and Rescue (COMSAR),
at its fourth session (12 to 16 July 1999), addressed that problem and developed such interim procedures, the
Maritime Safety Committee approved the interim MRCC/CS procedures upon reception of a DSC alert and
an Inmarsat alert, as set out in annexes 1 and 2, accordingly.
3 Member Governments are invited to use the annexed Interim MRCC/CS procedures and bring them
to the attention of all parties concerned.
***

MSC/Circ.959
I:\CIRC\MSC\959.doc
ANNEX 1
INTERIM PROCEDURES FOR MRCC ON RECEIPT OF A DSC DISTRESS ALERT
The procedure described below is a guidance, and should under no circumstances restrict the effort necessary
to confirm the safety of a vessel or persons onboard.
DISTRESS ALERT WHERE SHIP’S POSITION IS
INCLUDED
• The position is within own SRR Ø MRCC/CS to acknowledge the alert by DSC and
telephony.
• The position is outside own SRR. Ø Defer acknowledgement for a short period to allow
appropriate MRCC/CS to acknowledge. 
Ø If no acknowledgement, relay the alert to
appropriate MRCC.  Request acknowledgment.
DISTRESS ALERT WHERE SHIP’S POSITION IS NOT
INCLUDED
• The alert received via VHF. Ø MRCC/CS to acknowledge the alert by DSC and
telephony. Assume co-ordination.
Ø Attempt to ascertain the position.
• The alert received via MF or HF Ø Defer acknowledgement for a period.
Ø Check the MMSI/MID, acknowledge and attempt to
establish contact . 
Ø If response received, and in own SRR co -ordinate as
appropriate.  If in distress outside own SRR,
co-ordinate until appropriate MRCC assumes SMC.
Ø If no response received, continue investigating, but
also pass alert to the flag state /appropriate
MRCC/SAR data provider. Request
acknowledgement.
DISTRESS RELAY ALERT
• If transmitted by MRCC/CS Ø The distress relay alert shall not be acknowledged.
• If transmitted by a ship within own SRR. Ø MRCC/CS to acknowledge.
• If transmitted by a ship outside own SRR. Ø Pass alert to appropriate MRCC.  Request
acknowledgement.
• If transmitted by a ship without distress position. Ø Attempt to ascertain position and continue
investigating..
ALL SHIP URGENCY
• DSC urgency is an announcement of a call to be
transmitted via a given frequency.
Ø Do not acknowledge.
Ø Monitor given frequency.
DSC DISTRESS ALERT ACKNOWLEDGEMENT
• Received from a ship station Ø If original distress is not received, request distress
details from the acknowledging ship.
• Received from a MRCC/CS Ø Acknowledging MRCC/CS will be responsible for
the co-ordination.  If necessary seek additional
information.
***

MSC/Circ.959
I:\CIRC\MSC\959.doc
ANNEX 2
INTERIM MRCC/CS PROCEDURES UPON RECEPTION OF AN INMARSAT ALERT
The procedure described below is a guidance, and should under no circumstances restrict the effort necessary
to confirm the safety of a vessel or persons onboard.
DISTRESS ALERT
• The position is within own SRR. Ø Acknowledge the alert
Ø MRCC to assume co-ordination. 
• The position is outside own SRR. Ø Acknowledge the alert.
Ø MRCC to co-ordinate actions until appropriate
MRCC assumes SMC.
Ø Pass alert to appropriate MRCC.  Request
acknowledgement.
• Missing or not updated position. Ø Acknowledge the alert.
Ø MRCC to assume co-ordination.
Ø Check ID/MID, and pass information to
appropriate MRCC/SAR data provider/Flag
State. Request acknowledgement.
